title: Company decision scenario lab — Q3 prep
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight working notebook for the leadership + product-ops rehearsal ahead of the Q3 company cascade. Goal: converge on a compact set of company-level OKR hypotheses, a short list of failure-mode thresholds, and the all-hands framing we will use to signal tradeoffs and ask teams for concrete commits.

Context: quick bullets
- Growth in hosted usage has slowed vs Q1 projections; Dedicated pipeline is healthy but onboarding slippage exists.
- We need a tight set of company OKRs that prioritize reliability (SLOs), cost-per-token improvements, and an easier path for enterprise Private deals.
- This is intentionally a constrained planning exercise: pick 3 company-level OKRs, assign success metrics, and prepare 2 fallback scenarios.

Proposed company OKR hypotheses (drafts) — short, measurable
1) Reliability & Latency (Owner: SRE lead)
   Objective: End-user inference remains predictable under 99th percentile traffic spikes.
   Key Results (candidate):
   - KR1: 99th percentile tail latency <= 120ms for the top-3 enterprise routes across Hosted and Dedicated by end of Q3
   - KR2: Reduce P99 failure rate (502/timeout) by 50% vs baseline (Apr 2025)
   - KR3: Deploy two automated fallback routes (model variant + region) with canary test coverage for top 10 routes

2) Cost Efficiency (Owner: Infra + Optimize)
   Objective: Reduce per-token serving cost while preserving >95% signal fidelity on our eval sets.
   Key Results (candidate):
   - KR1: 20% reduction in per-token GPU cost for stateless text generation workloads via batching + quantization profiles
   - KR2: Prefix/KV cache hit rate >= 35% on targeted low-variance customer cohorts
   - KR3: Ship Optimize recommendations in Console for top 50 customers (by spend) with adoption tracking

3) Enterprise Private Traction (Owner: Sales + Private Deployments)
   Objective: Close and onboard regulated/private customers faster with predictable packages.
   Key Results (candidate):
   - KR1: 3 net-new Private deals closed with >=$150k ARR each
   - KR2: Reduce Private onboarding time from initial contract to production from median 12 weeks to 8 weeks
   - KR3: Deliver a hardened VPC deployment template + KMS integration tested with one reference customer

Notes on composition: keep Objectives short and action oriented. KRs should be binary where possible (or narrowly thresholded) to ease measurement.

Scenarios & decision thresholds
- Scenario A: Upside growth — usage rebounds + Dedicated demand surge
    Trigger: M-o-M hosted usage > +12% for 6 weeks and Dedicated committed capacity orders > forecast by 15%
    Decision: Accelerate Dedicated capacity hires, expand autoscale burst budget, delay deeper cost-optimization work by 2 quarters.
- Scenario B: Base case (expected)
    Trigger: Hosted usage within ±5% of forecast; Dedicated stable; Private funnel growing slowly
    Decision: Prioritize Reliability OKR and targeted Optimize recommendations; proceed with 1 Private reference onboarding.
- Scenario C: Downside pressure
    Trigger: Hosted usage < -10% vs forecast for 4 weeks OR churn of two top-10 customers
    Decision: Enact short-term cost containment (freeze noncritical infra spend), prioritize cost-per-token KR and defer major feature launches.

All-hands framing draft (60m) — rehearsal script points
- Opening (CEO, 7m): Quick context — one-line thesis for the quarter, why a tighter set of company OKRs helps (honest tradeoff framing).
- Product & Reliability update (VP Product + SRE, 12m): Current state, top 3 outages/learnings, what we will measure (show dashboards).
- OKR pitch (Maya / product-ops, 8m): Read the 3 proposed company OKRs + why these. Explicit asks to teams: commit 2–3 scoped team-level KRs that map to at least one company KR.
- Breakouts (20m): Pre-assigned cross-functional groups (PLs + Eng leads + Sales rep) to draft team-level commitments and identify blockers. Use Google Jamboard links.
- Consolidation (8m): Rapid readouts from breakouts, agree on owners and next steps.
- Q&A (5m): Pre-seeded questions from leadership Slack channel.

Pre-reads to circulate (48h before meeting)
- One-pager with the 3 OKRs and measurement plan (this doc condensed).
- SRE dashboard screenshots (latency/failure trends last 12 weeks).
- Private onboarding friction map (steps + current median times).

Risks, tradeoffs and guardrails
- Risk: Over-indexing on cost could degrade quality; guardrail = QA sample-based regression alerts with acceptance thresholds before enabling new quantization profiles for a cohort.
- Risk: Narrow OKRs may miss developer experience issues; include a qualitative pulse (developer NPS) as a watch metric.
- Guardrail: If any KR misses target by >25% at mid-quarter check, trigger a rapid replan (2-week leadership offsite).

Open questions (work-in-progress)
- Measurement: What exact metric will we use for "per-token GPU cost" (gross infra only, or include amortized infra+SRE ops)? Who owns this calc?
- Private deals: do we count contracted ARR at signed date or only after onboarding complete? Sales ops input needed.
- All-hands: Do we want pre-assigned breakout groups by org or cross-functional random grouping? Ops prefers pre-assigned to avoid coordination friction.

Immediate next steps (owners & deadlines)
- Maya: flatten this doc into a two-page pre-read for execs (due 2025-06-20) — ACTION: @Maya
- Aaron: produce P99 latency and failure rate baseline tables and a short slide (due 2025-06-16) — ACTION: @Aaron
- Priya: draft Private onboarding step-by-step map + friction metrics (due 2025-06-18) — ACTION: @Priya
- Tomás: prepare Jamboard templates and assign breakout groups (due 2025-06-19) — ACTION: @Tomás

Adjacency notes / helpful links

- Related RFC on quantization profiles: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/88 (linked).

Scratch / miscellaneous (notes to self)
- Keep the all-hands short — we want breakout action, not another update hour.
- Consider shipping a follow-up async Miro for teams that can't make the live breakouts.
